title: Reserved pool fragmentation after cross-region failover causing tenant burst shortfalls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent 429s and degraded throughput during regional failover windows. Investigation shows reserved-pool capacity was available overall but was functionally unusable for affected tenants due to slot fragmentation and stale affinity markers after a RAFT leader change in the autoscaler. This ticket tracks diagnosis, mitigation, and a patch to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate AZ/regional failover by draining replicas in region A and triggering leader re-election of the autoscaler controller. 2) Recreate tenant burst workload (short spikes with high concurrency). 3) Observe allocation skew: many small free slots in cold pools but no contiguous allocations matching tenant burst policies. 4) Verify KV cache affinity tags show stale node IDs and lease table contains entries with expired timestamps not reclaimed.
timeline: 2026-03-10: First customer escalation (FinLedger) opened support case reporting repeated 429s during scheduled maintenance. 2026-03-11: Pager alerted SRE; emergency triage. 2026-03-11 18:00 UTC: We applied rolling restart of autoscaler leaders to restore leadership, temporary improvement observed. 2026-03-12: Repro harness confirmed fragmentation after simulated failover. 2026-03-13: Root cause hypothesis refined; created this ticket and assigned to Miguel. 2026-03-14: Hotpatch PR opened and smoke-tested in staging.
mitigation_applied: Short term: temporarily increased per-tenant burst headroom to allow soft admission of burst requests for impacted customers and enabled conservative fallback routing to warm pools. SRE also rotated autoscaler leaders to flush stale leader state. Communications: support notified affected customers and set expectation for patch ETA.
root_cause: A race between lease deallocation and affinity re-tagging after controller leadership transitions. The allocator's scoring function preferred locality which, combined with partially-reclaimed slot fragments and a bug in lease garbage collection, left many small free segments that could not satisfy tenant burst allocation sizes. Additionally, telemetry missed a metric: fragmented_slot_ratio was not emitted during leader transitions due to a metrics-buffering regression.
proposed_fix: 1) Make lease deallocation idempotent and atomic with respect to the allocator index. 2) Add a compaction pass: allocator will coalesce adjacent free slots in reserved pools during leadership handover. 3) Adjust scoring to penalize fragmentation-heavy pools for large-burst admissions. 4) Re-enable fragmented_slot_ratio metric and add an alert on >15% fragmentation sustained for >5m.
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy patch to staging then to a single low-risk region for 6 hours with synthetic burst tests. If no regressions, expand to 25% of clusters over 12 hours, run customer smoke tests, then full rollout. Rollback: revert PR and scale fallback routing up immediately. Ops playbook updated at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DAR-alloc-compaction-playbook
tests: Unit: lease reclaim idempotency and compaction pass. Integration: simulated leader failover with heavy burst traffic (10k req/min) verifying no >1% increase in 429s. Load: soak test 24h across mixed tenants to validate no regression in tail latency.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: fragmented_slot_ratio (per-pool), compaction_runs_count, reclaimed_leases/sec. Alerts: fragmented_slot_ratio > 0.15 for 5m and 429 rate increase >200% for tenant with burst SLA. Dashboard: dedicated/autoscaler/fragmentation — link in artifacts.
stakeholders: SRE: Priya Nair, Platform Eng: Miguel Alvarez, Product: Jonas Becker, Support/CS: Emily Chen. Notified legal/compliance for customer communications as this affected regulated tenants.
customer_communication: Draft posted in support ticket: we identified a fragmentation bug in the reserved-pool allocator triggered by leadership transitions. Short-term mitigation in place; permanent patch planned and ETA 2026-03-18. We will offer credits for affected SLA windows. Legal approved messaging for enterprise customers.
action_items: 1) Complete PR reviews and merge hotpatch (Miguel) 2) Run full canary and customer smoke (SRE) 3) Add compaction metric and alert (Priya) 4) Postmortem and timeline for credits/comms (Emily) 5) Backport to maintenance branch for private on-prem builds (Platform Eng)
notes: This failure mode is distinct from prior 'burst-credit' accounting bugs: here capacity exists but is fragmented and the allocator cannot pack allocations efficiently. Avoid duplicating past fixes; ensure compaction does not introduce latency spikes — compaction should be bounded and rate-limited.
